items.entry_text: about 2 hours, Oct 2026
items.note_evidence: Notes give no tour duration or tour date (only that the notes were typed in chat on 30 Oct 2026).
items.fix: Remove 'about 2 hours' unless she confirms it; give the date as she states it.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: no clear front, entrance hard to find
items.note_evidence: Step 1: 'there's no like true front or arrival, and it was hard fj find the entrance'.
items.fix: None.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: perimeter fence with a video-and-voice intercom at the gate
items.note_evidence: Step 1: fence surrounded 'the whole thing'; step 2: 'buzz security at the fence and talk to them through a video and voice thing'.
items.fix: Optional: 'at the fence' (her words) rather than 'at the gate'.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: ramp up to a buzzed building door
items.note_evidence: Step 3: 'went up a ramp to the front door which they all had to buzz me in through'.
items.fix: None.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: vestibule with a guard behind glazing, an ID slot, screens and cameras
items.note_evidence: Step 4: guard 'in a closed off room with bullet proof glass', 'a little thing to slide my ID under', 'massive aceeens and cameras'.
items.fix: Acceptable softening of 'bullet proof' (she cannot verify a rating), but say 'glazing she describes as bullet-proof' so the detail is not lost; 'screens' rests on the 'aceeens' reading.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: visitor pass, buzzed door into a lobby
items.note_evidence: Step 5: 'They gave me a pass and buzzed me through the next door into a bright lobby'.
items.fix: Minor: she says 'a pass', not 'visitor pass'.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: client hot desks, private client offices, client kitchen and boardroom
items.note_evidence: Step 7, with her correction 'No I mean private client offices'; 'board room for climates' read as clients.
items.fix: None (location 'to the right, open to the lobby' omitted; see omitted).

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: washrooms with lockers and showers
items.note_evidence: Step 10: 'bathrooms with lockers and showers'.
items.fix: None. (The reason, 'some clients come over night', is correctly under claims.)

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: a technicians' room with two desks
items.note_evidence: Step 8: 'techniction room further down the hall with two guys desks and equipment'.
items.fix: Optional: add 'and equipment'.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: a POP room and meet-me room at the front right and another pair at the back left, behind scanner doors
items.note_evidence: Step 9: first pair 'in the far right side' and 'These rooms both required scanners'. Step 17: second pair reached after leaving by 'a back side door (back left corner)'; no scanners mentioned for the second pair.
items.fix: Say 'far right side' (not 'front right'); place the second pair off the hallway by the back-left exit; limit 'scanner doors' to the first pair unless she confirms the second.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: a single-person security portal that weighed and measured her
items.note_evidence: Step 12: 'I went in the glass circle and it weighed me and measured me'; photo shows 'a round glass security portal'.
items.fix: Flag: 'single-person' is inferred, not in notes. Ask her whether she knew it weighed/measured her from a display or because the guide said so; if the guide, move that function to GUIDE'S CLAIMS.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: a staff door with biometric and card
items.note_evidence: Step 11: 'He went through the RHS door with biometrics AND a scanner'.
items.fix: Use 'biometrics and a scanner' (she did not say card); 'staff' is inferred from the guide using it; note it is the right-hand door.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: a first-floor hall on an 18 in raised floor reached by a ramp
items.note_evidence: Step 13: 'an 18" raised floor above slab with a ramp to get up'.
items.fix: Flag to her: the raised floor and ramp are observed, but did she measure/estimate 18 in or was she told? If told, move the figure to GUIDE'S CLAIMS.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: three tenant enclosures with their own biometrics and cameras
items.note_evidence: Step 14 is wholly prefaced 'He said': 'only three tenants downstairs and they all had their own private enclosures with the company biometrics and cameras so I couldn't even see these servers'.
items.fix: Move the biometrics/cameras (and the tenant count) to GUIDE'S CLAIMS, or ask her whether she saw the enclosures and their readers herself (likely, since she 'couldn't see these servers'). Also: she wrote 'the company biometrics', which could mean Cologix's, not the tenants' own; do not say 'their own'.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: 400 A wall panels
items.note_evidence: Step 15: 'Than he should be the electrical boxes (400 A) on the wall' (read as 'he showed me').
items.fix: Use her words 'electrical boxes' (not 'panels', a more specific equipment type). Flag: whether 400 A was read off a label or said by the guide is unknown; the item depends on the 'he showed me' reading.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: VESDA
items.note_evidence: Step 15: 'the vesda fire thing'.
items.fix: None, though the identification as VESDA may have come from the guide (same 'he showed me' caveat).

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: a humidifier
items.note_evidence: Step 15: 'and a humidifier'.
items.fix: Same 'he showed me' caveat.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: a loading bay with two docks and a client delivery room
items.note_evidence: Step 18: 'loading bay with two docks and a private room where clients could have deliveries stored'.
items.fix: Minor: the room's purpose (client delivery storage) is something she could only know from the guide; consider marking the purpose as a claim.

items.entry_text: OBSERVED: a freight elevator to a second-floor hall
items.note_evidence: Step 19: 'a freight elevator off this room that went up to the second story (full floor of data hall'. Notes do not say she went up.
items.fix: Keep the freight elevator as OBSERVED; move 'goes to the second floor, which is a full data hall' to GUIDE'S CLAIMS unless she went up.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: anti-ram ('K') fence sunk about 9 ft
items.note_evidence: Step 1: 'surrounded by a K gate fence drilled 9 feet underground'. Not explicitly attributed to the guide, but she could not see underground, so the claims bucket is right.
items.fix: Flag: 'anti-ram' is the transcriber's reading of 'K gate' (K-rating); keep her term 'K gate fence' and mark 'anti-ram' as interpretation. Note it is unattributed in her notes.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: 24/7 guard
items.note_evidence: Step 4: '(24/7 guard)'. Unattributed, but not observable in one visit.
items.fix: None; note it is inferred as the guide's.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: three tenants on that floor
items.note_evidence: Step 14: 'He said there were only three tenants downstairs'.
items.fix: None.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: a sensor on every rack reporting temperature and humidity to an outside monitoring company
items.note_evidence: Step 16: 'Every server box has a sensor on it and it records temperature and humidity and reports to a third party who is constantly monitoring everything'. Unattributed, but she could not see the servers.
items.fix: Flag: 'rack' is a reading of 'server box'; keep her wording or confirm.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: the second POP is for redundancy
items.note_evidence: Step 17: 'another POP and meet me room for redundancy'.
items.fix: Say 'second POP and meet-me room'.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: some clients work overnight
items.note_evidence: Step 10: 'because some clients come over night'.
items.fix: Use 'some clients come in overnight' (she did not say they work).

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: power export 'is not a thing'
items.note_evidence: First message: giving power back to the grid 'is not a thing and would never make sense'.
items.fix: Quote is accurate but the reasons he gave are dropped (see omitted).

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: generator testing the only give-back
items.note_evidence: First message: 'the only realistic give-back is generator testing'.
items.fix: Restore 'realistic'.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: 2N (Cologix's page says N+1)
items.note_evidence: First message: 'multiple UPS systems and multiple feeds (2N), because they can't risk an outage'. Nothing about Cologix's page or N+1.
items.fix: Remove '(Cologix's page says N+1)' from the tour entry, or label it clearly as the transcriber's cross-check against a separate register source. Keep 'multiple UPS systems and multiple feeds'. Flag: whether '2N' was his term or her gloss is unclear.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: industry moving to liquid-to-chip cooling in a closed loop
items.note_evidence: 'he also said the industry was moving toward liquid (glycol) to chip cooling' and, separately, 'he kept saying it was a closed loop.'
items.fix: Restore '(glycol)'. Flag: 'it' in 'it was a closed loop' is unclear (could be this site's cooling, not liquid-to-chip); keep the two claims separate unless she confirms.

items.entry_text: GUIDE'S CLAIMS: data cabling mostly fibre now
items.note_evidence: 'they don't even use that much copper anymore and it's mostly fibre'.
items.fix: Minor: 'they' may mean this site rather than the industry; 'data cabling' is a reasonable gloss.

items.entry_text: One visit: observations, not measurements.
items.note_evidence: Editorial caveat, not a content claim.
items.fix: None.

omitted: Site description from her first message: converted industrial building, about 5 MW, multi-tenant colocation, outside-air free cooling plus magnetic-levitation chillers, Tier III (source of these facts unclear: guide, web, or her own; ask her).

The guide's reasons power export makes no sense: expensive and the amount would be insignificant; they can't even get enough power from the grid; even with onsite generation they'd always need a substation connection and power guarantees for clients; latency-sensitive clients would never agree to share; uptime is too important; maybe possible with a single tenant with consistent, predictable demand, but still insignificant.
'would never make sense' (second half of the power-export quote).
Redundancy detail: multiple UPS systems and multiple feeds, 'because they can't risk an outage'.
Guard is in a closed-off room; glass described as bullet-proof; screens described as massive.
Lobby is bright; photo contents: Cologix sign, sofa and chairs, round glass security portal, black door marked 'NOTICE ENTER HERE' with a card reader, glass meeting room with a 'RESERVED' sign.
Hot desk area is to the right of the lobby and open to it; offices, kitchen and boardroom are off it; she offered to draw it in plan later.
Technician room is further down the hall and has equipment.
First POP room has fibre running from the street.
Entry to the data hall is via the 'spinny door' from the lobby; the guide used the right-hand door.
She could not see the servers because of the tenant enclosures.
Exit from the data hall by a back side door in the back-left corner into a little hallway that serves the second POP/meet-me room and the loading bay.
Second storey is a full floor of data hall (only 'second-floor hall' kept).

interpretations.comment: Reasonable in context ('massive aceeens and cameras' in a security room). Low risk, but ask her to confirm.
Plausible autocorrect, but flag to her: it decides whether the 400 A boxes, VESDA and humidifier are OBSERVED, and whether '400 A' was his statement.
Reasonable; every other room in that sentence is for clients. Low risk.
